mainTopic: Whether visitors to a sick person can later act as judges, and until when a person may back out of a קנין (transaction)
overview: The amud opens by finishing a point about רב יהודה's rule on three people who visit a sick person. By day they may either write his will or judge the matter. At night they may only write, because by the next day they are already witnesses, and a witness cannot become a judge. רבה בר חנינא confirms that this is what he meant. The גמרא then brings a מחלוקת about how long a person may back out of a קנין. רבה says it is as long as the people are still sitting together, and רב יוסף says it is as long as they are still talking about that deal. רב יוסף tries to prove his view from רב יהודה's rule. If the sick man could still back out while everyone sits there, how could the visitors judge his case? רב אשי answers that the same problem exists for רב יוסף. Whatever answer רב יוסף gives can work for רבה too, and that argument finishes on the next amud.

steps.title: At night, even three visitors may write but not judge
steps.stepSummary: The speaker suggests that רב יהודה's rule only applies by day. At night even three visitors may only write, because they become witnesses, and a witness cannot become a judge.
steps.simpleTranslation: But at night, even three may write the will but may not judge. Why? Because they have already become witnesses, and a witness cannot become a judge.
steps.whatsHappening: The speaker (אביי) is checking his understanding of רב יהודה's rule. He suggests that at night, even three visitors may only write the will and may not judge.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A בית דין does not judge at night, so any judging would have to happen the next day. By then, the visitors already saw the matter at night as witnesses. Since a witness cannot become a judge in the same matter, they lose the option to judge.

keyTerms.meaning: They act as a court and judge
A witness cannot become a judge in the same case

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the rule that one person cannot be both witness and judge in the same matter.

phrases.english: But at night, even three
may write, but may not act in judgment.
What is the reason?
Because they have become witnesses,
and a witness cannot become a judge.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the discussion of רב יהודה's rule about three visitors to a sick person, which began before this section.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does the rule mean that at night, even three visitors may only write and not judge?

steps.title: Yes, that is exactly what I meant
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר חנינא confirms that this is exactly what he meant.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Yes, that is indeed what I am saying.
steps.whatsHappening: The other scholar agrees that the suggested understanding is correct.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Nothing new is added here. The suggestion from step 1 is simply confirmed: at night, the visitors become witnesses and cannot judge.

keyTerms.meaning: That is indeed what I am saying

steps.whatToRemember: By day, three visitors may write or judge. At night, they may only write, because they have become witnesses.

phrases.english: He said to him: Yes,
that is indeed what I am saying.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: אִין, הָכִי נָמֵי קָאָמֵינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers and confirms the question of step 1.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Yes, at night even three may only write and may not judge.

steps.title: How long can someone back out of a transaction?
steps.stepSummary: רבה and רב יוסף argue about how long after a קנין a person can still change his mind.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was stated: a קנין, until when can a person back out of it? רבה says: as long as they are still sitting there. רב יוסף says: as long as they are still dealing with that same topic.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new מחלוקת about how long a person may back out of a deal after making a קנין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבה measures the time by place: as long as the people are still sitting together. רב יוסף measures it by subject: as long as they are still talking about that deal. Under רב יוסף, changing the subject ends the right to back out, even if everyone is still sitting.

keyTerms.meaning: It was stated (introduces an argument between אמוראים)
A formal act that makes a transaction binding
As long as they are sitting

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the time window in which a binding deal can still be undone.

phrases.english: It was stated: a transaction,
until when can one back out?
Rabba says: as long as they are sitting.

phrases.aramaic: רַב יוֹסֵף אָמַר: כׇּל זְמַן שֶׁעוֹסְקִין בְּאוֹתוֹ עִנְיָן.
phrases.english: Rav Yosef says: as long as they are dealing with that matter.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new but related topic. It will be tied back to רב יהודה's rule.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבה: one can back out as long as the people are sitting. רב יוסף: one can back out as long as they are discussing that topic.

steps.title: רב יוסף proves his view from רב יהודה's rule
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף argues that רב יהודה lets the visitors judge right away. Under רבה's view, the sick man could still change his mind while they sit there, so judging would make no sense.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: Logic supports my view, because רב יהודה said: three who came to visit a sick person may write if they want, or judge if they want. If you think one can back out as long as they are sitting, we should worry that he might still change his mind!
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף brings רב יהודה's rule as a proof that his own view is correct and רבה's view is not.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the visitors can act as judges, the sick man's instructions must already be final. Under רבה, he could still back out as long as everyone is sitting, so the matter would not be settled. רב יוסף thinks his own view avoids this problem.

keyTerms.meaning: Let us worry that he may back out

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף: כְּווֹתִי דִּידִי מִסְתַּבְּרָא,
phrases.english: Rav Yosef said: It stands to reason like my view,
for Rav Yehuda said:
Three who entered to visit a sick person,
if they wish, they write; if they wish, they act in judgment.

phrases.aramaic: וְאִי סָלְקָא דַּעְתָּךְ כׇּל זְמַן שֶׁיּוֹשְׁבִין,
phrases.english: And if you think it is as long as they are sitting,
let us worry that perhaps he will back out!
phrases.notes: "He" is the sick man. How can they judge his case if he can still change his mind?

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף: כְּווֹתִי דִּידִי מִסְתַּבְּרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a proof for רב יוסף's side of the מחלוקת in step 3.
steps.raayaObject: רב יוסף's view that one can back out only while still discussing the topic
steps.raayaSupportSource: רב יהודה's rule that three visitors to a sick person may act as judges

steps.title: The same problem exists for רב יוסף
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי reports that he challenged the proof before רב כהנא. Even under רב יוסף, the sick man could back out while they are still discussing the matter.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: I said this teaching before רב כהנא and asked: Does it work out any better for רב יוסף? We should still worry that he might back out!
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי challenges רב יוסף's proof by showing that it causes the same problem for רב יוסף himself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under רב יוסף, a person can back out as long as the topic is still being discussed. So the sick man could also change his mind under רב יוסף's view. The proof does not favor רב יוסף over רבה.

keyTerms.meaning: I said this teaching before him

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב אָשֵׁי: אַמְרִיתַהּ לִשְׁמַעְתָּא קַמֵּיהּ דְּרַב כָּהֲנָא;
phrases.english: Rav Ashi said: I said this teaching before Rav Kahana;
and according to Rav Yosef, does it work out well?!
Let us also worry that perhaps he will back out!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the proof in step 4 by turning it back on רב יוסף.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב יוסף's proof from רב יהודה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Under רב יוסף, one can also back out while the topic is still being discussed, so the same worry applies to him.

steps.title: Whatever answer רב יוסף gives works for רבה too
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי starts to show that רב יוסף must explain the case as one where they already moved off the topic. That kind of answer can be used for רבה as well.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, what do you have to say? That they had moved away (from the topic)...
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי begins to explain how רב יוסף would answer his own problem. He is setting up the point that רבה can give the same kind of answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יוסף would have to say that רב יהודה's case is where the people already finished discussing the will. In the same way, רבה can say it is where they already got up. So the proof from רב יהודה does not decide the מחלוקת.

keyTerms.meaning: That they withdrew or moved on

steps.confusionAlert: This sentence is not finished yet. It continues on the next amud, where the גמרא gives the matching answer for רבה.
steps.whatToRemember: רב יהודה's rule does not prove רב יוסף right. Each side can explain it as a case where the time for backing out had already ended.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא מַאי אִית לָךְ לְמֵימַר – דִּיסְלִיקוּ
phrases.english: Rather, what must you say? That they withdrew
phrases.notes: He means they had already moved off the topic of the will. The sentence continues on the next amud.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows the way out of the step 5 problem, which also cancels רב יוסף's proof.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects רב יוסף's proof from רב יהודה
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The answer רב יוסף needs (that they moved on) can also be used by רבה (that they got up), so the proof proves nothing.
